cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?

mechanism: A grants harmless-looking factual questions and acknowledgments from above until B admits changing the picnic date, then assigns the consequence through another question.
confusable: D16 seeks confession before A disclosure; D40 specifically traces who altered an arrangement through innocent questions.
comparison: A calendar date and handwriting trail differ from the furniture alternative gradual admission of changed shared-space arrangements.
seedUse: Use D40-a canonical pen and handwriting clues only as creative context; its protected single exception remains untouched and is not approved by this pair assessment.
